     4	/-!
     5	# Games, tensor-product strategies, and value
     6	
     7	This file provides the finite game carrier used by the Pauli basis test.  Pure
     8	states are vectors in `EuclideanSpace`, and POVMs use the project's matrix
     9	`Measurement` structure.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:game`, `def:povm-conventions`,
    14	`def:tensor-product-strategy`, and `def:tensor-product-value` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:47-82` and `8-26`.
    16	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-57`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	/--
    27	A finite two-player one-round game with a probability distribution on question
    28	pairs and a Boolean decision predicate.  This is `def:game` in
    29	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:51-59`, with paper origin
    30	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:10-24`.
    31	-/
    32	structure Game where
    33	  QuestionA : Type
    34	  QuestionB : Type
    35	  AnswerA : Type
    36	  AnswerB : Type
    37	  [questionAFintype : Fintype QuestionA]
    38	  [questionBFintype : Fintype QuestionB]
    39	  [answerAFintype : Fintype AnswerA]
    40	  [answerBFintype : Fintype AnswerB]
    41	  [questionADecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionA]
    42	  [questionBDecidableEq : DecidableEq QuestionB]
    43	  [answerADecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerA]
    44	  [answerBDecidableEq : DecidableEq AnswerB]
    45	  μ : Distribution (QuestionA × QuestionB)
    46	  μ_prob : μ.IsProbability
    47	  decide : QuestionA → QuestionB → AnswerA → AnswerB → Bool
    48	
    49	attribute [instance] Game.questionAFintype Game.questionBFintype
    50	  Game.answerAFintype Game.answerBFintype Game.questionADecidableEq
    51	  Game.questionBDecidableEq Game.answerADecidableEq Game.answerBDecidableEq
    52	
    53	/--
    54	The marginal of a joint POVM obtained by post-processing its answer pair.  This
    55	is the POVM convention of `def:povm-conventions` in
    56	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; the post-processing operation
    57	is the already formalized `Measurement.postprocess`, with paper origin
    58	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    59	-/
    60	noncomputable def marginalLeft {α β d : Type*}
    61	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    62	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    63	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement α d :=
    64	  M.postprocess Prod.fst
    65	
    66	/-- The right marginal of a joint POVM, obtained using `Prod.snd` in
    67	`def:povm-conventions`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`,
    68	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
    69	-/
    70	noncomputable def marginalRight {α β d : Type*}
    71	    [Fintype α] [Fintype β] [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    72	    [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    73	    (M : Measurement (α × β) d) : Measurement β d :=
    74	  M.postprocess Prod.snd
    75	
    76	/-- Projectivity of every effect in a POVM (`def:povm-conventions`, blueprint
    77	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:8-26`; paper origin
    78	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:68-72`). -/
    79	def Measurement.IsProjective {α d : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    80	    (M : Measurement α d) : Prop :=
    81	  ∀ a, IsProj (M.effect a)
    82	
    83	/--
    84	The tensor-product strategy of `def:tensor-product-strategy` in
    85	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69` (paper origin
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`).
    87	-/
    88	structure Strategy (G : Game) where
    89	  ιA : Type
    90	  ιB : Type
    91	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA]
    92	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB]
    93	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA]
    94	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB]
    95	  ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA × ιB)
    96	  ψ_norm : ‖ψ‖ = 1
    97	  A : G.QuestionA → Measurement G.AnswerA ιA
    98	  B : G.QuestionB → Measurement G.AnswerB ιB
    99	
   100	attribute [instance] Strategy.ιAFintype Strategy.ιBFintype
   101	  Strategy.ιADecidableEq Strategy.ιBDecidableEq
   102	
   103	/-- The rectangular tensor placement used in strategy probabilities.  This is
   104	the finite-matrix realization of `def:tensor-product-strategy`, blueprint
   105	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:61-69`; paper origin
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:26-38`.
   107	-/
   108	def heteroKron {ιA ιB : Type*} (A : Op ιA) (B : Op ιB) : Op (ιA × ιB) :=
   109	  Matrix.kronecker A B
   110	
   111	/- The Euclidean linear map is the shared action used by the value and distance
   112	functionals.  Keeping it at the Euclidean-space level avoids accidentally
   113	using the function-space supremum norm of `Matrix.mulVec`. -/
   114	/-- Apply a finite matrix to a Euclidean-space state.  This is the Hilbert-space
   115	action underlying `def:tensor-product-value`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   117	noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   118	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
   119	  Matrix.toEuclideanLin M ψ
   120	
   121	/-- The Born weight of an answer pair for a strategy.  Lean-only support for
   122	`def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`. -/
   124	private noncomputable def outcomeWeight {G : Game} (S : Strategy G)
   125	    (x : G.QuestionA) (y : G.QuestionB) (a : G.AnswerA) (b : G.AnswerB) : ℝ :=
   126	  let M : MIPStarRE.Quantum.Op (S.ιA × S.ιB) :=
   127	    heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) ((S.B y).effect b)
   128	  let acted := applyOperatorToState M S.ψ
   129	  (inner ℂ S.ψ acted).re
   130	
   131	/--
   132	The tensor-product value, expressed as the distribution average of the Born
   133	probabilities.  This is `def:tensor-product-value` in
   134	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, with paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`.
   136	-/
   137	noncomputable def Strategy.value {G : Game} (S : Strategy G) : ℝ :=
   138	  avgOver G.μ (fun xy =>
   139	    ∑ a : G.AnswerA, ∑ b : G.AnswerB,
   140	      if G.decide xy.1 xy.2 a b then outcomeWeight S xy.1 xy.2 a b else 0)
   141	
   142	/--
   143	The tensor-product game value as a conditional supremum over all finite
   144	strategies.  The `sSup (Set.range ...)` form is the csSup formulation requested
   145	for `def:tensor-product-value`, blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:71-82`, paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:40-57`; attainment is
   148	intentionally not asserted here.
   149	-/
   150	noncomputable def Game.value (G : Game) : ℝ :=
   151	  sSup (Set.range (fun S : Strategy G => S.value))
   152	
   153	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	When a formalization relies on a cited mathematical source, the cited source
    20	should remain intact.  It is a source, not an errata file.  If a possible gap,
    21	missing hypothesis, incorrect numerical constant, or other mathematical
    22	discrepancy is found, the matter should be recorded in a separate LaTeX note.
    23	In this repository such notes live under \path{docs/paper-gaps/}.  The same
    24	principle applies when the formal development has already diverged from the
    25	cited source, for instance by changing a statement so that it compiles, or by
    26	using a different mathematical route because an available formal-library theorem
    27	has a slightly different form.  Such a note is a mathematical note first, and a
    28	record of the formalization second: it should be readable by a mathematician or
    29	mathematical physicist who has not followed the issue discussion.
    30	
    31	The note should isolate the mathematical mechanism.  It should say what the
    32	cited source asserts, what the cited results actually imply, where a term or
    33	hypothesis is lost, and what statement the formal development proves instead.
    34	If the formal proof takes a different route, the note should explain the
    35	replacement argument and the hypotheses on which it rests.  This is especially
    36	important when the proof uses a theorem, construction, or convention from
    37	Mathlib which is not part of the cited argument.  In that case the note should
    38	state the Mathlib result in ordinary mathematical language, explain how it is
    39	specialized to the notation of the paper, and compare its hypotheses and
    40	conclusion with the step it replaces.  It should not merely say that \Lean{} did
    41	not accept a proof, that the modified proof compiles, or that a named library
    42	lemma was applied.
    43	
    44	The documents in this directory should themselves follow this standard.  A
    45	policy or template which reads like a checklist will tend to produce checklist
    46	notes; the examples and templates should therefore be written as mathematical
    47	prose.
    48	
    49	\section{Concision and Readability}
    50	
    51	A paper-gap note should be short enough that a reader can understand the issue
    52	in one sitting.  The first page should answer four questions: what the source
    53	uses, how hard the remaining formal work is, what the formalization or audit
    54	checked, and what the current verdict is.  Begin with a short
    55	\emph{At a glance} section when the note concerns an open or recently resolved
    56	formalization task.  That section should estimate the difficulty, the rough
    57	implementation weight, the split between Mathlib reuse and project-local work,
    58	and the key Mathlib APIs or modules.  Use honest ranges, not false precision.
    59	
    60	The \emph{Key theorem forms} section should be Section~2, immediately after
    61	\emph{At a glance}.  Put the theorem forms before the source details so the
    62	reader knows what the formalization is aiming to prove.  After that, keep the
    63	source assertion, the mechanism being checked, the blueprint/formal comparison,
    64	and the conclusion.  Use more sections only when a counterexample or long
    65	derivation genuinely needs room.
    66	
    67	Keep background to the minimum needed for the local point.  Prefer one clear
    68	special case over a general restatement of the surrounding theorem.  Use displayed
    69	equations for the source assertion, the key calculation, and the theorem forms;
    70	avoid displays for traceability data, declaration names, or long lists.  The
    71	blueprint/formal comparison should be compact and should not repeat the theorem
    72	forms.  The section ``Form of the Note'' below specifies where traceability data
    73	belongs; the body should read as mathematical prose, not as a log.
    74	
    75	If the verdict is that there is no mathematical discrepancy, say so plainly and
    76	stop.  Keep the conclusion highly compact, normally under twenty source lines.
    77	If the only remaining work is an implementation task, name it briefly and link
    78	the issue or pull request in a footnote.
    79	
    80	\section{When the Investigation Starts}
    81	
    82	The investigation starts when the obstruction appears to be mathematical rather
    83	than merely formal.  No final judgement is needed at this stage.  It is enough
    84	that, after reading the relevant source and attempting the corresponding formal
    85	statement, the proof seems to require a different scalar, an additional
    86	hypothesis, a different tensor placement, a distinction between two objects which
    87	the prose identifies, or an auxiliary assertion not supplied by the cited
    88	argument.
    89	
    90	The same investigation should also start when such a deviation is discovered
    91	after the fact.  If the existing formal development or informal blueprint has
    92	already changed the statement, strengthened a hypothesis, weakened a conclusion,
    93	inserted an unadvertised lemma, or replaced the cited proof by a different
    94	formal-library argument, the mathematical change should be documented even if all
    95	relevant files already compile.
    96	
    97	At this early stage the purpose is to preserve the question while it is still
    98	local.  The note may later conclude that the matter is only notational, that an
    99	intermediate estimate in the cited source needs a harmless correction, that a
   100	missing hypothesis is genuinely needed, or that no discrepancy remains.  Thus
   101	the trigger is not the severity of the eventual verdict, but the appearance of a
   102	real mismatch between the cited reasoning and the statement that can be
   103	formalized.
   104	
   105	A failed tactic search, a missing formal lemma, or an inconvenient coercion is
   106	not enough.  The obstruction must survive translation back into ordinary
   107	mathematics.
   108	
   109	Sometimes an investigation uncovers an improvement that is not a discrepancy:
   110	the formalization works correctly, but it could be simplified by using an
   111	existing library, replacing a custom type, or adopting a cleaner proof route.
   112	These are not, by themselves, paper-gap notes.  They are action items.  When
   113	such an improvement is identified, open a GitHub issue or pull request that
   114	describes the proposed change.  If the investigation also produces a paper-gap
   115	note, link the issue or pull request from that note: the note records the
   116	mathematical justification, and the issue or pull request drives the
   117	implementation.
   118	
   119	\section{When to Write a Note}
   120	
   121	A note should be written once the source argument and the formal proof no longer
   122	match as mathematical arguments.  This includes, for instance, a numerical
   123	estimate whose constant does not follow from the cited lemma, a displayed
   124	conclusion which uses an unstated hypothesis, or a step in which two objects are
   125	identified although they must remain distinct.  In analytic, algebraic,
   126	probabilistic, or quantum arguments, such distinctions may concern the domain of
   127	a map, the placement of a tensor factor, the type of an outcome, the distinction
   128	between a structure and a substructure, or the scalar carried by an approximation
   129	relation.
   130	
   131	A note is required when an audit finds that a Lean declaration associated with a
   132	source-labelled statement has acquired an extra non-source hypothesis, such as
   133	bridge, residual, repair, producer, or obligation-structure data.  Such a
   134	declaration is temporary proof debt, not a replacement for the source theorem,
   135	and should not be introduced merely to avoid a \verb|sorry|.  The note must say
   136	plainly that the Lean result is conditional, identify the source-faithful theorem
   137	form that remains to be proved, and give the intended obligation discharger or
   138	removal plan.  The blueprint should not mark the source-labelled statement with
   139	\verb|\leanok| by pointing to this conditional helper.
   140	
   141	Changing a Lean theorem away from the statement in
   142	\path{references/ldt-paper/} is strongly discouraged.  A paper-gap note should
   143	not make such a change look routine: it should explain the mathematical
   144	necessity, or else classify the change as proof debt to be removed.
   145	
   146	When an existing conditional helper is audited, the first task is to extract any
   147	argument it already contains into source-faithful lemmas.  If the remaining
   148	bridge hypothesis cannot be derived from the paper hypotheses, the formal
   149	development should restore the source theorem statement and record the missing
   150	proof obligation explicitly, rather than retaining the strengthened statement as
   151	though it were the paper theorem.
   152	
   153	This requirement is not meant to classify every explicit Lean side condition as
   154	a discrepancy.  Positivity, nonemptiness, decidability, field-model instances,
   155	and denominator nonvanishing hypotheses may be faithful encodings of the domain
   156	in which the paper's theorem is stated.  The note should distinguish such
   157	boundary hypotheses from hypotheses that supply an unproved step of the paper
   158	argument.
   159	
   160	A note is also appropriate when the proof becomes formal only after changing an
   161	intermediate scalar, weakening a conclusion, strengthening a hypothesis, or
   162	inserting an additional lemma which is not simply an expansion of the cited
   163	argument.  These are mathematical changes, even when they are harmless for the
   164	final theorem.  It is likewise appropriate when an available formal-library
   165	theorem proves the needed result under a somewhat different formulation from the
   166	cited source.  In that case the note should be deliberately pedagogical.  It
   167	should explain, in ordinary mathematical language, what the replacement result
   168	says, how it is specialized, which hypotheses are new or differently packaged,
   169	and why the resulting statement is a legitimate substitute for the step in the
   170	cited argument.  If the issue remains open after reasonable attempts, the note
   171	should say what has been checked and what remains unknown.
   172	
   173	\section{Counterexamples}
   174	
   175	If the cited assertion appears to be false, the note should not stop at saying
   176	that the proof cannot be formalized.  It should give the counterexample, or the
   177	smallest relevant part of it, in ordinary mathematical notation.  The example
   178	should be accompanied by enough verification that the reader can see both sides:
   179	the hypotheses of the cited assertion hold, and its conclusion fails.

    26	\begin{definition}[Tensor product strategies]
    27	  \label{def:tensor-product-strategy}
    28	  A \emph{tensor product strategy} $\strategy$ for a game $\game = (\cal{X},
    29	  \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is a tuple $(\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ where
    30	  \begin{itemize}
    31		\item $\ket{\psi}$ is a pure quantum state, i.e.\ a unit vector in $\mH_A \otimes \mH_B$ for finite
    32	    dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $\mH_A, \mH_B$,
    33		\item $A$ is a set $\{A^x\}$ such that for every $x \in \cal{X}$, $A^x =
    34	    \{A^x_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is a POVM over $\mH_A$, and
    35		\item $B$ is a set $\{B^y\}$ such that for every $y \in \cal{Y}$, $B^y =
    36	    \{B^y_b \}_{b \in \cal{B}}$ is a POVM over $\mH_B$.
    37	\end{itemize}
    38	\end{definition}
    39	
    40	\begin{definition}[Tensor product value]
    41	  \label{def:tensor-product-value}
    42		The \emph{tensor product value} of a tensor product strategy $\strategy =
    43	  (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$  with respect to a game $\game=(\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A},
    44	  \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is defined as
    45	  \begin{equation*}
    46			\val^*(\game, \strategy) = \sum_{x,\, y,\, a,\, b} \, \mu(x,y)\, D(x,y,a,b)\,
    47	    \bra{\psi} A^x_a \otimes B^y_b\, \ket{\psi}\;.
    48	  \end{equation*}
    49		For $v\in[0,1]$ we say that the strategy $\strategy$ \emph{passes (or wins)
    50	    $\game$ with probability $v$ if} $\val^*(\game, \strategy) \geq v$.
    51	  The \emph{tensor product value} of $\game$ is defined as
    52	  \begin{equation*}
    53			\val^*(\game) = \sup_\strategy \val^*(\game, \strategy)\;,
    54	  \end{equation*}
    55		where the supremum is taken over all tensor product strategies $\strategy$ for
    56	  $\game$.
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	
    60	\begin{remark}
    61	  Unless specified otherwise, all strategies considered in this paper are tensor
    62	  product strategies, and we simply call them \emph{strategies}.
    63	  Similarly, we refer to $\val^*(\game)$ as the \emph{value} of the game
    64	  $\game$.
    65	\end{remark}
    66	
    67	
    68	\begin{definition}[Projective strategies]
    69	  \label{def:projective-strategy}
    70	  We say that a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ is \emph{projective} if
    71	  all the measurements $\{A^x_a\}_a$ and $\{B^y_b\}_b$ are projective.
    72	\end{definition}
    73	
    74	\begin{definition}\label{rem:symmetric-games}
    75		A game $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ is
    76	  \emph{symmetric} if the question and answer alphabets are the same for both
    77	  players (i.e.\
    78	  $\cal{X} = \cal{Y}$ and $\cal{A} = \cal{B}$), the distribution $\mu$ is
    79	  symmetric (i.e.\
    80	  $\mu(x,y) = \mu(y,x)$), and the decision predicate $D$ treats both players
    81	  symmetrically (i.e.\ for all $x,y,a,b$, $D(x,y,a,b) = D(y,x,b,a)$).
    82	 
    83	We call a strategy $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$
    84	  \emph{symmetric} if $\ket{\psi}$ is a (pure) state in $\mH \otimes \mH$, for some
    85	  Hilbert space $\mH$, that is invariant under permutation of the two factors,
    86	  and the measurement operators of both players are identical.
    87	\end{definition}
    88	
    89	We often specify symmetric games $\game$ and symmetric strategies $\strategy$ using
    90	  a compact notation: we write $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A}, \mu, D)$ and
    91	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, M)$ where $M$ denotes the set of measurement
    92	  operators for both players.
    93	
    94	\begin{lemma}\label{lem:symmetric-strat}
    95	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{A},  \mu, D)$ be a symmetric game
    96	  such that $\val^*(\game) = 1-\eps$ for some $\eps\geq 0$.
    97	  Then there exists a symmetric and projective strategy
    98	  $\strategy=(\ket{\psi},M)$ such that $\val^*(\game,\strategy)\geq 1-\eps$.
    99	\end{lemma}
   100	
   101	\begin{proof}
   102	  By definition for any $\eps'>\eps$ there exists a strategy $\strategy'= (\ket{\psi'},A,B)$ such
   103	  that $\val^*(\game,\strategy')\geq 1-\eps'$.
   104	Using Naimark's theorem (Theorem~\ref{thm:naimark}) we can assume
   105	without loss of generality that $\ket{\psi'}\in\C_{\alice'}^d\otimes \C_{\bob'}^d$ for some integer $d$
   106	  and that for every $x$, $A^x$ and $B^x$ are projective measurements.
   107	Let
   108	  \[
   109	    \ket{\psi} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \big( \ket{0}_\alice \ket{1}_\bob
   110	    \ket{\psi'}_{\alice'\bob'} + \ket{1}_\alice \ket{0}_\bob
   111	    \ket{\psi'_\tau}_{\alice'\bob'}\big) \in (\C_{\alice}^2 \otimes
   112	    \C_{\alice'}^d) \otimes (\C_\bob^2 \otimes \C_{\bob'}^d)\;,
   113	  \]
   114	  where $\ket{\psi'_\tau}$ is obtained from $\ket{\psi}$ by permuting the two
   115	  players' registers.
   116	  Observe that $\ket{\psi}$ is invariant under permutation of $\alice\alice'$
   117	  and $\bob\bob'$.
   118	
   119	  For any question $x\in \cal{X}$ define the measurement $M^x = \{M^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$
   120	  acting on the Hilbert space $\C^2 \otimes \C^d$ as follows:
   121	  \[
   122	  	M^x_a = \ketbra{0}{0} \otimes A^x_a + \ketbra{1}{1} \otimes B^x_a \;,
   123	  \]
   124		i.e.\ for $\ket{\varphi} \in \C^d$, $M^x_a(\ket{0}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{0}A^x_a\ket{\varphi}$ and $M^x_a(\ket{1}\ket{\varphi})=\ket{1}B^x_a\ket{\varphi}$.
   125	  When Alice receives question $x$, she measures $M^x$ on registers $\alice \alice'$, and when Bob receives 
   126	  question $y$, he measures $M^y$ on registers $\bob \bob'$.
   127	Using that by assumption the decision predicate $D$ for $\game$ is symmetric,
   128	  it is not hard to verify that $\val^*(\game,\strategy) =
   129	  \val^*(\game,\strategy')$.
   130	\end{proof}

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:comm-strategy}
   134	  Let $\game = (\cal{X}, \cal{Y}, \cal{A}, \cal{B}, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let
   135	  $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\game$ such that  $\mH_A = \mH_B$.
   136	  Let $S \subseteq \cal{X} \times \cal{Y}$ denote the support of the question
   137	  distribution $\mu$, i.e.\ the set of $(x,y)$ such that $\mu(x,y)>0$.
   138	  We say that $\strategy$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\game$} if for all
   139	  question pairs $(x, y) \in S$, we have $[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0$ 
   140	  for all $a
   141	  \in \cal{A}, b \in \cal{B}$, where $[A, B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   142	\end{definition}
   143	
   144	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]
   145	  \label{def:consistent-measurement}
   146	  Let $\cal{A}$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$ be a
   147	  state, and let $\{ M_a \}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ be a projective measurement on
   148	  $\mH$.
   149	  We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if
   150	  and only if
   151	  \begin{equation*}
   152	    \forall a \in \mA\;,\quad M_a \otimes \Id_\bob\, \ket{\psi}
   153	    = \Id_\alice \otimes M_a\, \ket{\psi}\;.
   154	  \end{equation*}
   155		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent}.
   156	\end{definition}
   157	
   158	The terminology ``consistent'' arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is 
   159	\[ \sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \otimes M_a \ket{\psi}\,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} \,=\, \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_\alice \otimes M_a \ket{\psi} \,=\,1\;,\]
   160	where the first equality is by definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a=\Id$. 
   161	
   162	\begin{definition}[Consistent strategies]
   163	  \label{def:consistent-strategy}
   164		Let $\strategy = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a projective strategy with state
   165	  $\ket{\psi} \in \mH \otimes \mH$, for some Hilbert space~$\mH$, which is
   166	  defined on question alphabets $\cal{X}$ and~$\cal{Y}$ and answer alphabets
   167	  $\cal{A}$ and~$\cal{B}$, respectively.
   168	  We say that the strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in
   169	  \cal{X}$, the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \cal{A}}$ is consistent on
   170	  $\ket{\psi}$ and if for all $y \in \cal{Y}$, the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in
   171	    \cal{B}}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   172	\end{definition}
   173	
   174	We almost always restrict our attention to symmetric strategies. In this case, consistency implies that whenever both players are sent the same question, they provide the same answer. 
   175	
   176	\begin{definition}
   177	  \label{def:spcc}
   178	  We say that a strategy $\strategy$ for a game $\game$ is \emph{PCC} if it is projective, consistent, and commuting for $\game$.
   179	  Additionally, we say that a PCC strategy $\strategy$ is \emph{SPCC} if it is furthermore symmetric.
   180	\end{definition}

    61	\begin{definition}[Tensor product strategies]\label{def:tensor-product-strategy}
    62		\uses{def:game, def:povm-conventions}
    63		A \emph{tensor product strategy} $\mathcal S$ for a game $\mathfrak G = (\mathcal X, \mathcal Y, \mathcal A, \mathcal B, \mu, D)$ is a tuple $(\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ where
    64		\begin{itemize}
    65			\item $\ket{\psi}$ is a pure quantum state, i.e.\ a unit vector in $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ for finite-dimensional complex Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_A$, $\mathcal H_B$,
    66			\item $A$ is a set $\{A^x\}$ such that for every $x \in \mathcal X$, $A^x = \{A^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal A}$ is a POVM on $\mathcal H_A$, and
    67			\item $B$ is a set $\{B^y\}$ such that for every $y \in \mathcal Y$, $B^y = \{B^y_b\}_{b \in \mathcal B}$ is a POVM on $\mathcal H_B$.

    71	\begin{definition}[Tensor product value]\label{def:tensor-product-value}
    72		\uses{def:tensor-product-strategy}
    73		The \emph{tensor product value} of a tensor product strategy $\mathcal S = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ with respect to a game $\mathfrak G = (\mathcal X, \mathcal Y, \mathcal A, \mathcal B, \mu, D)$ is
    74		\[
    75			\operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G, \mathcal S) = \sum_{x,\,y,\,a,\,b} \mu(x,y)\, D(x,y,a,b)\, \bra{\psi} A^x_a \ot B^y_b \ket{\psi}\,.
    76		\]
    77		For $v \in [0,1]$ we say that the strategy $\mathcal S$ \emph{passes (or wins) $\mathfrak G$ with probability $v$} if $\operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G, \mathcal S) \ge v$. The \emph{tensor product value} of $\mathfrak G$ is
    78		\[
    79			\operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G) = \sup_{\mathcal S} \operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G, \mathcal S)\,,
    80		\]
    81		where the supremum is taken over all tensor product strategies $\mathcal S$ for $\mathfrak G$.
    82	\end{definition}

The principal case is that in which $\{M^x_a\}$ and $\{N^x_a\}$ are POVMs on $\mathcal H$, and we then speak of the state-dependent distance between the POVMs; but the relation is used for arbitrary operator families --- for instance for products of measurement operators, or for commutators compared against the identically zero family, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:commutation-analysis} below.
   226	\end{definition}

   228	\begin{definition}[Distance between strategies]\label{def:strategy-distance}
   229		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.AreCloseStrategies}
   230		\leanok
   231		\uses{def:tensor-product-strategy, def:state-distance, def:povm-distance}
   232		Let $\mathfrak G = (\mathcal X, \mathcal Y, \mathcal A, \mathcal B, \mu, D)$ be a nonlocal game and let $\mathcal S = (\psi, A, B)$ and $\mathcal S' = (\psi', A', B')$ be strategies for $\mathfrak G$. For $\delta \in [0,1]$ we say that \emph{$\mathcal S$ is $\delta$-close to $\mathcal S'$} if the following conditions hold.
   233		\begin{enumerate}
   234			\item The states $\ket{\psi}, \ket{\psi'}$ are states in the same Hilbert space $\mathcal H_A \ot \mathcal H_B$ and are $\delta$-close.
   235			\item For all $x \in \mathcal X$ and $y \in \mathcal Y$, we have $A^x_a \approx_\delta (A')^x_a$ and $B^y_b \approx_\delta (B')^y_b$, with the approximations holding under the distribution $\mu$ (i.e.\ under its corresponding marginals), on either $\ket{\psi}$ or $\ket{\psi'}$.
   236		\end{enumerate}
   237	\end{definition}

   239	\begin{remark}[Asymptotic reading of the distance relations]\label{rem:asymptotic-distance}
   240		Definitions~\ref{def:state-distance}, \ref{def:consistency}, and \ref{def:povm-distance} are asymptotic: every $\approx_\delta$ and $\simeq_\delta$ statement refers to families of states and measurement families indexed by an implicit parameter $n \in \N$, and the $O(\cdot)$ is taken as $n \to \infty$. None of these relations is a pointwise inequality with an explicit constant. By contrast, the corresponding relations used in the low individual degree chapters (Definitions~\ref{def:simeq} and~\ref{def:approx_delta}) carry no hidden constant. Any explicit quantitative version of the present relations therefore retains the constants absorbed into the $O(\cdot)$; for instance, the triangle inequality of Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle} carries a factor $2$ inside the $O(\cdot)$.

    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)

    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else

    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)

    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- Lean-only unfolding lemma for the unit-alphabet specialization of
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl

    58	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:212-219`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`.

    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Explicit equality of Alice's local spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Explicit equality of Bob's local spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))

   137	\begin{remark}[Attainment in the symmetrization lemma]\label{rem:symmetric-strat-limit}
   138		The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:symmetric-strat} yields, for each $\eps' > \eps$, a symmetric projective strategy of value at least $1-\eps'$. The conclusion as stated, at $\eps' = \eps$, does not follow from this: the dilated dimension $d$ may grow as $\eps' \downarrow \eps$, and the supremum defining $\operatorname{val}^*(\mathfrak G)$ in Definition~\ref{def:tensor-product-value} need not be attained by any strategy. The symmetrization construction itself is value-preserving, so the conclusion does hold whenever the hypothesis supplies an actual strategy of value at least $1-\eps$ rather than only the value of the game; every use of the lemma in the source proceeds from such a strategy, or from a strict lower bound on the value, and therefore consumes only what the proof establishes. The gap and the available repairs are documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_symmetrization-attainment}.
   139	\end{remark}

   141	\begin{definition}[Commuting strategies]\label{def:comm-strategy}

   143		\leanok
   144		\uses{def:game, def:tensor-product-strategy}
   145		Let $\mathfrak G = (\mathcal X, \mathcal Y, \mathcal A, \mathcal B, \mu, D)$ be a game, and let $\mathcal S = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy for $\mathfrak G$ such that $\mathcal H_A = \mathcal H_B$. We say that $\mathcal S$ is a \emph{commuting strategy for $\mathfrak G$} if for all question pairs $(x,y)$ in the support of $\mu$ (i.e.\ all $(x,y)$ with $\mu(x,y) > 0$) we have
   146		\[
   147			[A^x_a, B^y_b] = 0 \qquad \text{for all } a \in \mathcal A,\ b \in \mathcal B\,,
   148		\]
   149		where $[A,B] = AB - BA$ denotes the commutator.
   150	\end{definition}

   152	\begin{definition}[Consistent measurements]\label{def:consistent-measurement}
   153		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsConsistentOn}
   154		\leanok
   155		\uses{def:povm-conventions}
   156		Let $\mathcal A$ be a finite set, let $\ket{\psi} \in \mathcal H \ot \mathcal H$ be a state, and let $\{M_a\}_{a \in \mathcal A}$ be a projective measurement on $\mathcal H$. We say that \emph{$\{M_a\}_{a \in \mathcal A}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$} if and only if
   157		\[
   158			\forall a \in \mathcal A\,, \qquad M_a \ot \Id_B\, \ket{\psi} = \Id_A \ot M_a\, \ket{\psi}\,.
   159		\]
   160		When the state $\ket{\psi}$ is clear from context we simply say that $\{M_a\}_{a \in \mathcal A}$ is consistent.
   161	\end{definition}
   162	
   163	The terminology arises from the fact that when the measurement $\{M_a\}$ is performed on both registers of $\ket{\psi}$, the probability of obtaining twice the same outcome is
   164	\[
   165		\sum_a \bra{\psi} M_a \ot M_a \ket{\psi} = \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_A \ot (M_a)^2 \ket{\psi} = \sum_a \bra{\psi} \Id_A \ot M_a \ket{\psi} = 1\,,
   166	\]
   167	where the first equality is by the definition of consistency, the second uses that $\{M_a\}$ is projective, and the last uses $\sum_a M_a = \Id$.

We say that $\mathcal S$ is \emph{consistent} if for all $x \in \mathcal X$ the measurement $\{A^x_a\}_{a \in \mathcal A}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$, and for all $y \in \mathcal Y$ the measurement $\{B^y_b\}_{b \in \mathcal B}$ is consistent on $\ket{\psi}$.
   174	\end{definition}

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions
     5	
     6	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
     7	graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
     8	map to that seed.  The inductive predicate below records the level structure
     9	needed by later formalization stages.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`, `def:cl-dist`, `lem:cl-concat`, and
    14	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-535`.
    15	The paper origin is `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`
    16	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    24	
    25	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    26	
    27	/--
    28	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    29	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    30	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    31	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    32	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    33	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    34	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`,
    35	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    36	-/
    37	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    38	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    39	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    40	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    41	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    42	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    43	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    44	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    45	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    46	
    47	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    48	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    49	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:441-463`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    51	-/
    52	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    53	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    54	
    55	/-- Evaluation of a conditionally-linear syntax term.  Lean-only support for
    56	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    58	-/
    59	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    60	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    61	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    62	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    63	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    64	      fun x =>
    65	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    66	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    67	
    68	/-- The support invariant for a conditionally-linear syntax term.  This is a
    69	Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    70	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    71	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    72	-/
    73	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    74	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    75	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    76	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    77	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    78	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    79	
    80	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    81	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    82	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`, paper origin
    83	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    84	-/
    85	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    86	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    87	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    88	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,

    90	
    91	/--
    92	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    93	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`; paper
    94	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    95	-/
    96	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    97	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
    98	
    99	/--
   100	The distribution obtained by applying two conditionally linear maps to a common
   101	uniform seed.  This is `def:cl-dist` in
   102	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:467-470`, paper origin
   103	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:132-138`.
   104	-/
   105	noncomputable def clDistribution [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
   106	    (L R : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
   107	    Distribution ((ι → K) × (ι → K)) :=
   108	  (uniformDistribution (ι → K)).map (fun z => (L z, R z))
   109

   111	coordinates carry `L`, while the right coordinates carry the family member

   115	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:315-364`.
   116	-/
   117	def condLinearConcat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]
   118	    [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] (L : (ιU → K) → (ιU → K))
   119	    (R : (ιU → K) → (ιV → K) → (ιV → K))
   120	    (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) : ιU ⊕ ιV → K :=
   121	  let u : ιU → K := fun i => x (.inl i)

   126	Concatenating an outer and an indexed inner CL map adds their levels.  This is

   129	The direct-sum coordinate bookkeeping is represented by `condLinearConcat`; the

   131	-/
   132	theorem IsCondLinearOn.concat {ιU ιV : Type*} [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU]

   137	    (hR : ∀ u : ιU → K, u ∈ Set.range L →

   148	The underlying graph-distribution definition is

   150	-/
   151	noncomputable def graphDistribution {T : Type*} [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T]
   152	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (_hE : E.Nonempty) : Distribution (T × T) :=
   153	  Distribution.uniformOnFinset

     5	# Qubit form of Pauli basis test soundness
     6	
     7	The fixed self-dual normal basis converts the qudit EPR register and generalized
     8	Pauli projectors into qubit coordinates. The conversion uses only the basis
     9	stored in the canonical `FixedFieldModel`.

    11	## References
    12	
    13	The conversion is `lem:pauli-binary` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:675-708`, from
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. The resulting
    16	`cor:pauli-binary` is in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:409-435`,
    17	from `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1501`.
    18	-/

    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix

    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT

    26	noncomputable section
    27	
    28	/-- The bit register obtained by expanding every Pauli-register field element
    29	in the basis stored by `P.model`. -/
    30	abbrev QubitRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    31	  Cube P.m × Fin P.model.basisDim → ZMod 2
    32	
    33	/-- The ideal auxiliary state tensored with the qubit EPR register, in the
    34	local-player ordering used by `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
    35	noncomputable def idealQubitState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    36	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    37	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    38	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    39	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    40	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    41	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv
    42	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    43	    (fun p =>
    44	      (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    45	        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (QubitRegister P × QubitRegister P) ℂ
    46	          (eprState (QubitRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    47	
    48	/-- Existential data in `cor:pauli-binary`; this Lean-only package introduces
    49	no hypothesis beyond the paper theorem. -/
    50	structure QubitSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
    51	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
    52	  ιA' : Type
    53	  ιB' : Type
    54	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
    55	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
    56	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
    57	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
    58	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    59	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P)
    60	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    61	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P)
    62	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
    63	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
    64	
    65	attribute [instance] QubitSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype
    66	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype QubitSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq
    67	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
    68	
    69	/-- Alice's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    70	noncomputable def qubitProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    71	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    72	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    73	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    74	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    75	  fun p q =>
    76	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    77	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.1.2 q.1.2
    78	    else 0
    79	
    80	/-- Bob's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    81	noncomputable def qubitProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    82	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    83	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    84	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    85	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    86	  fun p q =>
    87	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
    88	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.2.2 q.2.2
    89	    else 0
    90	
    91	/-- Lift a conjugated Alice effect to the full qubit target space. -/
    92	noncomputable def liftedQubitAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
    93	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    94	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    95	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    96	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P))
    97	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
    98	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    99	  heteroKron (conjIsometry φA M) 1
   100	
   101	/-- Lift a conjugated Bob effect to the full qubit target space. -/
   102	noncomputable def liftedQubitBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   103	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   104	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   105	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   106	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P))
   107	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   108	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   109	  heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB M)
   110	
   111	/-- Alice's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   112	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceA
   113	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   114	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   115	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   116	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   117	      (liftedQubitAEffect S w.φA
   118	          ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   119	        qubitProjOnA'' P W u)
   120	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   121	
   122	/-- Bob's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   123	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceB
   124	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   125	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   126	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   127	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   128	      (liftedQubitBEffect S w.φB
   129	          ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   130	        qubitProjOnB'' P W u)
   131	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   132	
   133	/-- `cor:pauli-binary`: soundness of the Pauli basis test in qubit
   134	coordinates. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:409-435`, paper
   135	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1501`.
   136	
   137	The theorem retains the source-compatible nonnegative error boundary and uses
   138	only `P.model` and its stored basis dimension. -/
   139	theorem pauli_soundness_qubit :
   140	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   141	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   142	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   143	          ∃ w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S,
   144	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealQubitState P w.aux‖ ≤
   145	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   146	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   147	              qubitOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤
   148	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   149	            ∀ W : PauliKind,
   150	              qubitOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤
   151	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q := by
   152	  sorry
   153	
   154	end

    30	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;

    36	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *

   481	The \emph{trace of\/ $\F_{q^k}$ over\/ $\Fq$} is defined as
   482	\begin{equation}\label{eq:def-trace}
   483	  \tr_{q^k \to q} :\; a \,\mapsto \, \Tr(K_a)
   484	\end{equation}

   487	By definition, the trace is an $\Fq$-linear map from $\F_{q^k}$ to
   488	$\Fq$. The trace is in fact independent of the choice of basis, which
   489	can be seen from the following equivalent definition~\cite[Definition 2.1.80]{mullen2013handbook}:
   490	\[
   491		\tr_{q^k \to q}(a) = \sum_{j = 0}^{k-1} a^{q^j}\;.
   492	\]

   494	A \emph{dual basis} $\{e_1', e_2', \ldots, e_k' \}$ of $\{e_1, e_2, \ldots,
   495	e_k\}$ is a basis such that $\tr_{q^k \to q}(e^{}_i e'_j) = \delta_{i,j}$ for
   496	all $i, j \in \{1, 2, \ldots, k\}$.
   497	A \emph{self-dual basis} is one that is equal to its dual.
   498	If for some $\alpha \in \F_{q^k}$ the set $\{ \alpha^{q^j} \}_{j=0}^{k-1}$ forms a
   499	basis of $\F_{q^k}$ over $\Fq$, the basis is called a \emph{normal

   410	Quantum soundness of a version of the classical low-degree test for polynomials of low \emph{total} degree was claimed
   411	in~\cite{natarajan2018low}, building on an analysis of a three-prover version of the test in~\cite{vidick2016three}. Unfortunately there is a gap in the soundness analysis of this test.    414	  \label{lem:ld-soundness}

   419	  projective strategies $(\psi,A,B)$ that succeed with probability at least
   420	  $1-\eps$ in the game $\game^\ld_\ldparams$, there exists measurements
   421	  \[G^w \in \simulpolymeas{m}{d}{q}{\ldc}\] on $\mH_w$, for
   422	  $w\in\{\alice,\bob\}$, such that
   423	  \begin{equation*}
   424	    \begin{split}
   425	      A^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}
   426	      & \abc[\delta_{\ld}]
   427	      G^\bob_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}\;,\\
   428	      G^\alice_{[(g_1(u),g_2(u),\ldots,g_\ldc(u)) = (a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots \,,\, a_\ldc)]}

   430				 B^{\Point,\, u}_{a_1,\, a_2,\, \ldots\,,\, a_\ldc}\;,\\

   444	where $m, d, \ldc \in \N$ are integers, $q \in \N$ is an admissible field size,
   445	and $m$ divides $q$. Let $\Sigma=\F_q$. Let $\code \subseteq \Sigma^q$ be the Reed-Solomon code with degree $d$.    465	\subsubsection{Complexity of the classical low-degree test.}
   466	The CL functions and decision procedure of the low-degree test are incorporated
   467	as subroutines in some of the normal form verifiers constructed in subsequent
   468	sections.
   469	The next lemma establishes the time complexity of these procedures as a function
   470	of the parameter tuple $\ldparams = (q,m,d,k)$.
   471	The lemma also establishes the time complexity of computing the {description} of
   472	the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ as a Turing machine, given the parameter
   473	tuple $\ldparams$ as input.
   474	
   475	
   476	
   477	\begin{lemma}[Complexity of the classical low-degree test]
   478	  \label{lem:ld-complexity}
   479	  Let $\ldparams = (q,m,d,k)$ denote a parameter tuple.
   480	  \begin{enumerate}
   481		\item The time complexity of the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$
   482	    parametrized by $\ldparams$ is $\poly(m, d, k, \log q)$.
   483		\item The time complexity of evaluating marginals of the CL functions
   484	    $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$, and $L_\DLine$ at a given input point is $\poly(m, \log
   485	    q)$.
   486		\item The Turing machine description of the decision procedure $\decider^\ld$
   487	    parametrized by $\ldparams$ can be computed from $\ldparams$ in $\polylog
   488	    (q,m,d,k)$ time.
   489	  \end{enumerate}
   490	\end{lemma}

    69		Two subspaces $S$ and $T$ of a linear space $V$ form a pair of
    70		\emph{complementary subspaces} of $V$ if

    77		onto $T$ parallel to $S$). The unique linear map $L : V \to V$ with
    78		$x \mapsto x^S$ is the \emph{projector onto $S$ parallel to $T$}.

    31	      ((Distribution.uniformOnFinset s).toPMF

     4	# Finite-field bases and the fixed binary representation
     5	
     6	The Pauli basis test uses fields of size `2^k` for odd `k`, together with a
     7	chosen self-dual normal basis over `ZMod 2`.  This file records that choice as
     8	data, while exposing Mathlib's basis and algebra-trace APIs for later proofs.

   356	\begin{lemma}[Approximate commutation from joint consistency]\label{lem:commutation-analysis}
   357		\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.opDistSq_commutator_le}
   358		\leanok
   359		\uses{def:povm-distance, def:povm-conventions}
   360		Let $\{A^x_{a,\,b}\}$, $\{B^x_{a,\,b,\,c}\}$, $\{C^x_{a,\,c}\}$ be POVMs. Suppose $\{B^x_{a,\,b,\,c}\}$ is projective, and
   361		\begin{align*}
   362			A^x_{a,\,b} \ot \Id_B &\approx_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_{a,\,b}\,,\\
   363			C^x_{a,\,c} \ot \Id_B &\approx_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_{a,\,c}\,,
   364		\end{align*}
   365		where $B^x_{a,\,b} = \sum_c B^x_{a,\,b,\,c}$ and $B^x_{a,\,c} = \sum_b B^x_{a,\,b,\,c}$ are the marginals of Definition~\ref{def:povm-conventions}. Then the following approximate commutation relation holds:
   366		\[
   367			[A^x_{a,\,b},\, C^x_{a,\,c}] \ot \Id_B \approx_\delta 0\,.
   368		\]
   369	\end{lemma}
   370	\begin{proof}
   371		\uses{fact:add-a-proj, fact:triangle}
   372		Applying Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to $C^x_{a,\,c} \ot \Id_B \approx_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_{a,\,c}$ with the multiplier family $\{A^x_{a,\,b} \ot \Id_B\}$, we have
   373		\begin{equation}\label{eq:commutation-analysis-1}
   374			A^x_{a,\,b}\, C^x_{a,\,c} \ot \Id_B \approx_\delta A^x_{a,\,b} \ot B^x_{a,\,c}\,.
   375		\end{equation}
   376		Similarly, applying Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to $A^x_{a,\,b} \ot \Id_B \approx_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_{a,\,b}$ with the multiplier family $\{\Id_A \ot B^x_{a,\,c}\}$, and using that $\{B^x_{a,\,b,\,c}\}$ is projective,
   377		\begin{equation}\label{eq:commutation-analysis-2}
   378			A^x_{a,\,b} \ot B^x_{a,\,c} \approx_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_{a,\,c}\, B^x_{a,\,b} = \Id_A \ot B^x_{a,\,b,\,c}\,.
   379		\end{equation}
   380		Combining \eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-1} and \eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-2} via Lemma~\ref{fact:triangle},
   381		\begin{equation}\label{eq:commutation-analysis-3}
   382			A^x_{a,\,b}\, C^x_{a,\,c} \ot \Id_B \approx_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_{a,\,b,\,c}\,.
   383		\end{equation}
   384		A symmetric argument gives
   385		\begin{equation}\label{eq:commutation-analysis-4}
   386			C^x_{a,\,c}\, A^x_{a,\,b} \ot \Id_B \approx_\delta \Id_A \ot B^x_{a,\,b,\,c}\,.
   387		\end{equation}
   388		The claim follows by subtracting \eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-3} and \eqref{eq:commutation-analysis-4}.
   389	\end{proof}

   485	Conditionally linear functions specify the question distributions of the games considered in the following chapters in a form that can be ``introspected''. Intuitively, a conditionally linear function takes as input an element $x \in V = \F^n$ and applies linear maps $L_j$ sequentially to $x^{V_j}$, where $V_1, V_2, \dots$ is a sequence of complementary register subspaces such that both the linear map $L_j$ and the subspace $V_j$, for $j \ge 2$, may depend on the values taken by the previous linear maps $L_1(x^{V_1})$, $L_2(x^{V_2})$, and so on.

     2	import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.Basic
     3	
     4	/-!
     5	# Generalized Pauli operators and EPR states
     6	
     7	The definitions here use finite matrix entries and rank-one projectors, so they
     8	are usable by the later game statements without introducing an abstract
     9	operator algebra.  The Fourier/orthogonality identities are retained as named
    10	proof obligations for subsequent stages.
    11	
    12	## References
    13	
    14	The source-facing nodes are `def:lin-reg`, `def:EPR`, `def:generalized-pauli`,
    15	and `lem:pauli-observable-expansion` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:494-652`.  The paper origin is
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:908-1161`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	open scoped BigOperators Matrix ComplexOrder
    21	
    22	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    23	
    24	open MIPStarRE.Quantum
    25	
    26	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    27	  [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    28	
    29	/-- The two generalized Pauli bases used by the test in `def:generalized-pauli`,
    30	blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    31	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    32	-/
    33	inductive PauliKind where
    34	  | X
    35	  | Z
    36	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    37	
    38	/-- The binary character used for generalized Pauli phases; see
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1081`.
    40	
    41	It is public because the Fourier expansion declarations below expose this
    42	character in their statement types. -/
    43	noncomputable def phaseSign (t : ZMod 2) : ℂ :=
    44	  if t = 0 then 1 else -1
    45	
    46	/--
    47	The shift operator `τ^X(a)`.  Blueprint `def:generalized-pauli`,
    48	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`; paper origin
    49	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    50	-/
    51	noncomputable def tauShift (a : K) : Op K :=
    52	  fun i j => if i = j + a then 1 else 0
    53	
    54	/--
    55	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is
    56	the second operator of `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 529-571; paper
    57	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`).
    58	-/
    59	noncomputable def tauPhase (b : K) : Op K :=
    60	  fun i j => if i = j then phaseSign (binTrace K (b * j)) else 0
    61	
    62	/-- The single-qudit eigenvector coordinate used in the tensor-product basis;
    63	see `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1126-1161`. -/
    64	private noncomputable def singlePauliVec (W : PauliKind) (e x : K) : ℂ :=
    65	  match W with
    66	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0
    67	  | .X =>
    68	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))
    69	
    70	/--
    71	The normalized single/multi-qudit eigenvector for a Pauli basis label.  For an
    72	index type `ι`, the input `e : ι → K` labels the tensor-product basis vector.
    73	This is the vector form of `def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint
    74	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:550-570`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def pauliVec {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    78	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=
    79	  ∏ i : ι, singlePauliVec W (e i) (x i)
    80	
    81	/--
    82	The rank-one projector onto `pauliVec W e`.  This is the projective measurement
    83	element `τ^W_e` in `def:generalized-pauli` (blueprint lines 562-570; paper
    84	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1101-1122`).
    85	-/
    86	noncomputable def pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    87	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    88	  Matrix.vecMulVec (pauliVec W e) (fun x => star (pauliVec W e x))
    89	
    90	/-- A compact operator-valued form of a generalized Pauli observable from
    91	`def:generalized-pauli`, blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:529-571`, paper origin
    92	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1052-1096`.
    93	-/
    94	noncomputable def tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    95	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) : Op (ι → K) :=
    96	  fun x y =>
    97	    ∏ i : ι,
    98	      match W with
    99	      | .X => tauShift (a i) (x i) (y i)
   100	      | .Z => tauPhase (a i) (x i) (y i)
   101	
   102	/--
   103	The EPR vector on a finite label space.  Blueprint `def:EPR`,
   104	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:513-523`; paper origin
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`.
   106	-/
   107	noncomputable def eprState (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   108	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (V × V) :=
   109	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv (V × V) ℂ).symm
   110	    (fun p : V × V =>
   111	      if p.1 = p.2 then (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card V : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ else 0)
   112	
   113	/-- The EPR vector is normalized on a nonempty finite carrier; see
   114	`def:EPR`, `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:946-955`. -/
   115	theorem eprState_norm (V : Type*) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] [Nonempty V] :
   116	    ‖eprState V‖ = 1 := by
   117	  sorry
   118	
   119	/--
   120	Fourier expansion of a generalized Pauli observable in the Pauli projectors.
   121	This is `lem:pauli-observable-expansion`, equations `eq:pauli-obs-proj` and
   122	`eq:pauli-inversion-0`, in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`;
   123	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   124	Both directions are deliberately left as proof-level obligations in stage 4.1.
   125	-/
   126	theorem tauObservable_eq_sum_pauliProj {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   127	    (W : PauliKind) (a : ι → K) :
   128	    tauObservable W a =
   129	      ∑ e : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • pauliProj W e := by
   130	  sorry
   131	
   132	/-- The inverse Fourier expansion of a Pauli projector
   133	(`lem:pauli-observable-expansion`), blueprint
   134	`ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:638-652`, paper origin
   135	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1141-1161`.
   136	-/
   137	theorem pauliProj_eq_avg_tauObservable {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) :
   139	    pauliProj W e =
   140	      (Fintype.card (ι → K) : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   141	        ∑ a : ι → K, phaseSign (binTrace K (dotProduct a e)) • tauObservable W a := by
   142	  sorry
   143	
   144	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   653	\subsubsection{Bit string representations}
   654	\label{sec:ff-representations}
   655	
   656	As mentioned at the end of \Cref{sec:tms}, we sometimes treat the
   657	inputs and outputs of Turing machines as representing elements of a finite
   658	field, or a vector space over a finite field.
   659	We discuss some important details about bit representations of finite field
   660	elements and arithmetic over finite fields.
   661	
   662	In the paper we only consider fields $\F_{2^k}$ where $k$ is odd. 
   663	
   664	\begin{definition}\label{def:admissible-size}
   665	  A field size $q$ is called an \emph{admissible} field size if $q=2^k$ for odd
   666	  $k$.
   667	\end{definition}
   668	
   669	Elements of $\F_2$ are naturally represented using bits. 
   670	To represent elements of $\F_{2^k}$ as binary strings we require the
   671	specification of a basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$.
   672	Given a basis $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ of $\F_{2^k}$, every element $a \in \F_{2^k}$
   673	has a unique expansion $a = \sum_{i=1}^k a_i e_i$ and can be represented as the
   674	$k$-bit string corresponding to $\downsize(a) \in \F_2^k$.
   675	Note that we omitted the subscript $2$ of $\downsize$ as it maps to the linear
   676	space over the prime subfield $\F_2$.
   677	Thus the \emph{binary representation} of $a \in \F_{2^k}$ is defined as the
   678	natural binary representation of $\downsize(a) \in \F_2^k$ (which in turn is the
   679	\emph{$\F_2$-representation of $a$}).
   680	Throughout the paper we freely associate between the binary representation of a
   681	field element $a \in \F_{2^k}$ and its $\F_2$-representation,
   682	although---technically speaking---these are distinct objects.
   683	
   684	Given the representations $\downsize(a), \downsize(b)$ of $a, b \in \F_{2^k}$, to
   685	compute the binary representation of $a+b$ it suffices to compute the addition
   686	bit-wise, modulo $2$.
   687	Computing the multiplication of elements $a, b$ requires the specification of
   688	the multiplication tables $\{K_{e_i} \in \Matrix_k (\F_2)\}_{i=1}^k $ for the
   689	basis $\{e_i\}$.
   690	Given representations $\downsize(a) = (a_i)_{i=1}^k$, $\downsize(b) =
   691	(b_i)_{i=1}^k$ for $a, b \in \F_{2^k}$ respectively, the representation
   692	$\downsize(ab)$ of the product $ab$ is computed as
   693	\begin{equation}
   694	  \label{eq:eq-mult}
   695	  \downsize(ab) = \sum_{i=1}^k \, a_i \, \downsize \bigl( e_i b \bigr) =
   696	  \sum_{i=1}^k \, a_i \bigl( K_{e_i}\, \downsize (b) \bigr)\;.
   697	\end{equation}
   698	Thus, using our representation for field elements, efficiently performing finite
   699	field arithmetic in $\F_{2^k}$ reduces to having access to the multiplication
   700	table of some basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$.
   701	
   702	The following fact provides an efficient deterministic algorithm for computing a
   703	self-dual normal basis for $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$ and the corresponding
   704	multiplication tables for any odd $k$.
   705	
   706	\begin{lemma}
   707	  \label{lem:efficient_basis}
   708	  There exists a deterministic algorithm that given an odd integer $k > 0$,
   709	  outputs a self-dual normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$ and the
   710	  multiplication tables of the basis in $\poly(k)$ time.

     5	# Qubit form of Pauli basis test soundness

     7	The fixed self-dual normal basis converts the qudit EPR register and generalized
     8	Pauli projectors into qubit coordinates. The conversion uses only the basis
     9	stored in the canonical `FixedFieldModel`.

    11	## References
    12	
    13	The conversion is `lem:pauli-binary` in
    14	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:675-708`, from
    15	`references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex:1163-1208`. The resulting
    16	`cor:pauli-binary` is in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:409-435`,
    17	from `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1501`.

    28	/-- The bit register obtained by expanding every Pauli-register field element
    29	in the basis stored by `P.model`. -/
    30	abbrev QubitRegister (P : AdmissibleParams) :=
    31	  Cube P.m × Fin P.model.basisDim → ZMod 2
    32	
    33	/-- The ideal auxiliary state tensored with the qubit EPR register, in the
    34	local-player ordering used by `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
    35	noncomputable def idealQubitState (P : AdmissibleParams)
    36	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    37	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    38	    (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')) :
    39	    EuclideanSpace ℂ
    40	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    41	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv
    42	      ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) ℂ).symm
    43	    (fun p =>
    44	      (EuclideanSpace.equiv (ιA' × ιB') ℂ aux (p.1.1, p.2.1)) *
    45	        (EuclideanSpace.equiv (QubitRegister P × QubitRegister P) ℂ
    46	          (eprState (QubitRegister P)) (p.1.2, p.2.2)))
    47	
    48	/-- Existential data in `cor:pauli-binary`; this Lean-only package introduces
    49	no hypothesis beyond the paper theorem. -/
    50	structure QubitSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
    51	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
    52	  ιA' : Type
    53	  ιB' : Type
    54	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
    55	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
    56	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
    57	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
    58	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    59	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P)
    60	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    61	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P)
    62	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
    63	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
    64	
    65	attribute [instance] QubitSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype
    66	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype QubitSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq
    67	  QubitSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
    68	
    69	/-- Alice's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    70	noncomputable def qubitProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    71	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    72	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    73	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    74	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    75	  fun p q =>
    76	    if p.1.1 = q.1.1 ∧ p.2 = q.2 then
    77	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.1.2 q.1.2
    78	    else 0
    79	
    80	/-- Bob's ideal qubit projector placed on the joint target space. -/
    81	noncomputable def qubitProjOnB'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
    82	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    83	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB'] (W : PauliKind)
    84	    (u : PauliRegister P) :
    85	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    86	  fun p q =>
    87	    if p.1 = q.1 ∧ p.2.1 = q.2.1 then
    88	      qubitPauliProj W (kappaVec P.model u) p.2.2 q.2.2
    89	    else 0
    90	
    91	/-- Lift a conjugated Alice effect to the full qubit target space. -/
    92	noncomputable def liftedQubitAEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
    93	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
    94	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    95	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
    96	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × QubitRegister P))
    97	    (M : Op S.ιA) :
    98	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
    99	  heteroKron (conjIsometry φA M) 1
   100	
   101	/-- Lift a conjugated Bob effect to the full qubit target space. -/
   102	noncomputable def liftedQubitBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   103	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   104	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   105	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   106	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × QubitRegister P))
   107	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   108	    Op ((ιA' × QubitRegister P) × (ιB' × QubitRegister P)) :=
   109	  heteroKron 1 (conjIsometry φB M)
   110	
   111	/-- Alice's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   112	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceA
   113	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   114	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   115	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   116	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   117	      (liftedQubitAEffect S w.φA
   118	          ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   119	        qubitProjOnA'' P W u)
   120	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   121	
   122	/-- Bob's qubit-projector family distance in `cor:pauli-binary`. -/
   123	noncomputable def qubitOperatorDistanceB
   124	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   125	    (w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   126	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   127	    ‖applyOperatorToState
   128	      (liftedQubitBEffect S w.φB
   129	          ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   130	        qubitProjOnB'' P W u)
   131	      (idealQubitState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   132	
   133	/-- `cor:pauli-binary`: soundness of the Pauli basis test in qubit
   134	coordinates. Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:409-435`, paper
   135	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1450-1501`.
   136	
   137	The theorem retains the source-compatible nonnegative error boundary and uses
   138	only `P.model` and its stored basis dimension. -/
   139	theorem pauli_soundness_qubit :
   140	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   141	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   142	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   143	          ∃ w : QubitSoundnessWitness P S,
   144	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealQubitState P w.aux‖ ≤
   145	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   146	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   147	              qubitOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤
   148	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   149	            ∀ W : PauliKind,
   150	              qubitOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤
   151	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q := by
   152	  sorry
   153	
   154	end
   155	
   156	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

   172	/-- The quantitative error function in `lem:ld-soundness`.  Its argument order
   173	is `(a, b, ε, q, m, d, k)`. -/
   174	noncomputable def deltaLd (a b ε : ℝ) (q m d k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   175	  a * Real.rpow (((d * m * k : ℕ) : ℝ)) a *
   176	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
   177	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   178

   109	/-- Lift a conjugated B-side effect to the full ideal register in `thm:pauli`,
   110	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   111	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   112	-/
   113	noncomputable def liftedBEffect {P : AdmissibleParams} {G : Game}
   114	    (S : Strategy G) {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']
   115	    [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
   116	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   117	      EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   118	    (M : Op S.ιB) :
   119	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=
   120	  fun p q =>
   121	    if p.1 = q.1 then
   122	      (conjIsometry φB M) p.2 q.2
   123	    else 0
   124	
   125	/-- A finite witness packaging the auxiliary dimensions, isometries, and state
   126	from `thm:pauli`.  This structure is a Lean-only encoding of the existential
   127	data in the paper theorem; it introduces no extra hypothesis.  Blueprint
   128	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, paper origin
   129	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   130	-/
   131	structure PauliSoundnessWitness (P : AdmissibleParams)
   132	    (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P)) where
   133	  ιA' : Type
   134	  ιB' : Type
   135	  [ιAFintype : Fintype ιA']
   136	  [ιBFintype : Fintype ιB']
   137	  [ιADecidableEq : DecidableEq ιA']
   138	  [ιBDecidableEq : DecidableEq ιB']
   139	  φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   140	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P)
   141	  φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   142	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P)
   143	  aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')
   144	  aux_norm : ‖aux‖ = 1
   145	
   146	attribute [instance] PauliSoundnessWitness.ιAFintype PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBFintype
   147	  PauliSoundnessWitness.ιADecidableEq PauliSoundnessWitness.ιBDecidableEq
   148	
   149	/-- The A-side operator-distance quantity appearing in the soundness
   150	conclusion.  It is the finite-sum realization of `def:povm-distance` from
   151	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   152	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   153	-/
   154	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceA
   155	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   156	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   157	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   158	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedAEffect S w.φA
   159	        ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   160	      pauliProjOnA'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   161	
   162	/-- The symmetric B-side operator-distance quantity from `def:povm-distance`,
   163	blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`, paper origin
   164	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`.
   165	-/
   166	noncomputable def pauliOperatorDistanceB
   167	    (P : AdmissibleParams) (S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P))
   168	    (w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S) (W : PauliKind) : ℝ :=
   169	  ∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   170	      ‖applyOperatorToState (liftedBEffect S w.φB
   171	        ((S.B (pauliQuestion P W)).effect (.pauliOutcome u)) -
   172	      pauliProjOnB'' P W u) (idealState P w.aux)‖ ^ 2
   173	
   174	/-- `thm:pauli`: every sufficiently successful Pauli basis test strategy admits
   175	local isometries and an auxiliary unit state for which the state and both
   176	operator families are close at scale `deltaQld`.  The theorem uses the
   177	once-and-for-all self-dual-normal field model selected by `fixedFieldModel` for
   178	each admissible size, rather than a freshly quantified field identification.
   179	Blueprint
   180	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`; paper origin
   181	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.
   182	
   183	The paper's asymptotic constants are encoded by the explicit `deltaQld`
   184	functional; the squared operator distances use the quantitative convention of
   185	`def:povm-distance` (`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:201-220`).
   186	-/
   187	theorem pauli_soundness :
   188	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   189	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) (ε : ℝ), 0 ≤ ε →
   190	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   191	          ∃ w : PauliSoundnessWitness P S,
   192	            ‖isometryTensor w.φA w.φB S.ψ - idealState P w.aux‖ ≤
   193	                deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   194	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   195	              pauliOperatorDistanceA P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) ∧
   196	            (∀ W : PauliKind,
   197	              pauliOperatorDistanceB P S w W ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q) := by
   198	  sorry
   199	
   200	end
   201	
   202	end MIPStarRE.QPBT
